newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce plans GDR issue.
newsitem.headline: Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce plans GDR issue.

text.p: Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce plans to increase its capital through an issue of Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) and a domestic share offering, according to a statement published in Beirut newspapers.
It did not indicate the size of the capital increase but banking sources in Beirut put it at $50-60 million.
The bank will be the third Lebanese bank to raise capital on the international market following a GDR issue by Banque Audi and a private placement by Byblos Bank, both in 1995.

The statement said the GDRs would be listed on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange and the shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange, making the bank the first in Lebanon to offer shares simultaneously on the local and international markets.

Nomura International had been appointed global coordinator for the capital increase and the Middle East Capital Group (MECG), a new Beirut merchant banking house, had been named lead manager for the Middle East, the statement said.
Officials at Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce and MECG declined requests for more details of the capital proposed issues.
The bank is Lebanon's oldest commercial bank, founded in 1950. It has 30 active branches in Lebanon, the second biggest network in the country, and 443 employees.
